title: Dual-Channel Oscilloscope Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav's meter reads 7 V from a small adapter. But is that voltage steady, or wobbling up and down? A meter gives one number. To see the shape, he needs an oscilloscope. This animated lesson builds the cathode ray oscilloscope piece by piece and then puts a dual-channel scope to work.

Inside the cathode ray tube: the heated cathode, the control grid (brightness), the anodes (speed and focus), the Y plates (the signal moves the spot up and down), the X plates driven by the sawtooth time base, the phosphor screen and the trigger that makes the picture stand still. Then how one beam shows two channels in alternate mode and chop mode, and a live breadboard where CH1 and CH2 probe an RC circuit and the output shrinks and lags as the frequency rises. We read the screen with VOLTS/DIV and TIME/DIV, find peak-to-peak voltage, period, frequency and phase difference, and work a full example (8 V peak to peak, 1 kHz). Then the exam trap (peak vs peak to peak), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 21 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 3: Measuring Instruments (Karnataka PUC Electronics).
